_readme: The interaction gate: walk up to an NPC, press the button, and check control actually
changed hands - then that it comes back.
This needs the whole game at once. The player's facing decides who is addressed, the
Router decides whether input is accepted, and the dialog box decides when it is over -
and only pressing a real button through the real input map exercises all three.
The conversation is closed with press_until_state rather than with a fixed number of
presses. Counting presses would tie this gate to how many LINES the writer put in the
dialog, so adding a sentence would break a test about control handover - and pressing
one time too many simply re-opens the conversation, leaving the gate reporting the
very state it was trying to leave.

steps.text: a new game starts with nothing promised to anyone
spawn is tile (4,6); the kid stands at (8,8)

press through the conversation until control comes back
